NDT training in Lake Charles: how it works for Lake Charles employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Lake Charles and Southwest Louisiana employers and technicians, live online or onsite at your facility or yard. We provide the classroom training; your employer's written practice governs on-the-job experience, general, specific and practical exams administered by an ASNT Level III, vision tests and certification. Courses cover UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I and II, plus Level III preparation.

Southwest Louisiana has one of the most concentrated clusters of LNG export, refining and petrochemical plants in North America, stretched along the Calcasieu Ship Channel from Lake Charles and Westlake down to Cameron Parish and across to Sabine Pass. That density means constant demand for NDT: new-build construction on LNG trains and cracker units, maintenance turnarounds at operating plants, pipeline tie-ins, storage tank work and post-hurricane repair. It also means competition for qualified technicians is intense, and employers here care a great deal about how quickly a new hire can be productive on a code job.

Atlantis has no physical training centre in Lake Charles. We train your people through live-virtual classes and onsite sessions at your shop, yard or site facility, under ASNT Level III oversight. Request a Lake Charles training quote; cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Lake Charles

Courses follow ASNT SNT-TC-1A and the ANSI/ASNT CP-105 topical outlines. Level I and II cover principles, equipment, calibration, technique, code interpretation and reporting; Level III preparation adds depth and the basic examination.

MethodLevelsWhat Lake Charles employers use it forPrerequisite

Lake Charles contractors typically want Level II technicians in UT and RT first, then PAUT and TOFD as clients push to replace radiography with advanced UT on construction and turnaround work. Book a Level III consultation to plan the right sequence for your crew.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Lake Charles, step by step

Louisiana regulates radiation safety, but it does not issue general NDT certifications. Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you:

  1. Employer written practice defining training, experience, exams and certification. See written practice development.
  2. Classroom training for the hours your written practice requires, online or onsite with Atlantis. Recommended hours are in the training requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience, documented under qualified supervision on real jobs.
  4. General examination on method principles.
  5. Specific examination on your employer's procedures and the codes you work to, such as ASME Section V and B31.3.
  6. Practical examination on real flawed specimens, graded by a Level III or designated examiner.
  7. Vision examination at least annually.
  8. Certification by the employer after Level III review.
  9. Recertification per the written practice interval.

More on the framework: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Lake Charles crews

Southwest Louisiana work is scheduled around turnarounds and construction milestones, and the region's calendar also has to allow for hurricane season, which runs from June through November. Pulling a crew away at the wrong time can cost a contract. Atlantis offers:

  • Live online classroom for theory and Level III preparation, often run in the evenings or between shifts. See online NDT training.
  • Onsite at your facility in Lake Charles, Sulphur, Westlake or anywhere in the region, under ASNT Level III oversight, using your equipment and specimens.
  • Blended, theory online and practicals onsite, which lets you keep crews on the job during busy periods.

Tell us your spring and fall turnaround windows and any storm-recovery commitments, and we plan around them. Ask about onsite training for your Lake Charles crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Lake Charles

LNG export terminals

Southwest Louisiana and the adjacent Texas border host several operating LNG export terminals, and further export projects are under construction or development in Calcasieu and Cameron parishes. New-build LNG work involves huge volumes of process piping to ASME B31.3, cryogenic stainless and nickel-alloy welds, and full-containment storage tanks built to standards such as API 620 and API 625. PT, RT, UT and PAUT are all heavily used, and weld-inspection throughput is often the pace-setter on construction schedules.

Refining and petrochemicals

The Lake Charles and Westlake industrial corridor includes major refineries, ethylene crackers, polymer plants and chlor-alkali facilities. Maintenance turnarounds bring UT thickness surveys, PAUT, ET on heat exchangers, MT and PT on vessels and rotating equipment, and VT everywhere. Owner-user inspection programmes commonly follow API 510, 570 and 653 for vessels, piping and tanks; those inspector certifications are separate from NDT certification, and Atlantis does not train to them, but the NDT work underneath them is exactly what our courses cover.

Pipelines

Gas and liquids pipelines feed the LNG and petrochemical plants from across the Gulf Coast. Construction and tie-in work uses RT and automated UT to API 1104 and ASME B31.8. Operator qualification requirements are handled separately by the operator.

Port and marine

The Port of Lake Charles and the Calcasieu Ship Channel generate dock, crane, structural and marine work. Port and plant access typically requires a TWIC card and site safety orientation, which employers arrange.

Hurricane recovery and fabrication

After the major 2020 storms, repair and rebuilding work showed how much inspection capacity the region needs at short notice. Local fabrication shops produce piping spools, structural steel and pressure equipment, working to ASME Section VIII, B31.3 and AWS D1.1.

Construction work versus turnaround work

Lake Charles technicians tend to move between two very different kinds of job. On new-build construction, the work is volume-driven: thousands of welds, clear acceptance criteria in the construction code, and a daily push to keep inspection from holding up the welders. Radiography crews often work nights to stay clear of other trades, and PAUT is increasingly specified to replace RT so work can continue around the inspection. On turnarounds at operating plants, the work is condition-driven: finding and sizing corrosion, cracking and damage in equipment that has been in service for years, with tight windows and a lot of scaffolding. That calls for strong thickness gauging, flaw-sizing skills, clean data recording and the judgement to escalate findings quickly to the owner's inspector. Good training for this region prepares technicians for both, and that is how we structure practical exercises for Southwest Louisiana crews.

Radiography licensing in Louisiana

Louisiana is an NRC Agreement State. Industrial radiography is licensed by the Louisiana Department of Environmental Quality, and Louisiana is one of the states that runs its own industrial radiographer certification. Anyone performing industrial radiography must hold a valid industrial radiographer certification recognised by LDEQ, having completed the required radiation safety training and on-the-job training, and must work under a licensed company with a radiation safety officer. Atlantis RT courses teach the NDT method; the state radiation safety training and certification is separate and runs through your employer's licensed programme and the LDEQ process. Always check current requirements with LDEQ.

What Lake Charles employers typically ask for

  • SNT-TC-1A Level II certification in UT and/or RT, with complete records.
  • Advanced UT (PAUT, TOFD) for construction and turnaround work.
  • Knowledge of ASME Section V, Section VIII, B31.3 and API 1104.
  • A current Louisiana industrial radiographer card for RT crews.
  • TWIC and site safety orientation, arranged by the employer.
  • Some owners also ask for API inspector or welding inspector credentials; Atlantis does not train to those schemes.

For pay context see the NDT salary guide.

A practical first-year plan for new NDT technicians in Southwest Louisiana

People entering NDT in Lake Charles often come from welding, pipefitting, insulation or scaffolding crews already working in the plants. That background is an advantage: they know plant safety culture, permits and how a turnaround runs. What they need is a structured route into inspection. The plan below is typical for a trainee hired by a Southwest Louisiana inspection contractor; the exact order and requirements always come from the employer's written practice.

  1. Weeks one to four: site access and fundamentals. The employer arranges TWIC, site safety orientation and drug and alcohol screening. The trainee starts VT and PT Level I classroom training, often live online in the evenings, and shadows certified technicians on real jobs to start logging experience.
  2. Months two to four: add MT and UT thickness. Carbon steel weld inspection with MT and basic UT thickness gauging are the quickest routes to being useful on a turnaround. Classroom training for MT and UT Level I follows, with hands-on sessions onsite on the contractor's own blocks and specimens.
  3. Months four to eight: first Level I and Level II certifications. Once the experience hours in the written practice are met, the Level III administers general, specific and practical exams. VT, PT and MT are usually the first Level II certifications a Lake Charles trainee earns.
  4. Months six to twelve: UT shear wave or RT. This is where the career branches. Trainees who show aptitude for UT move toward shear-wave weld inspection and later PAUT and TOFD. Those who go into radiography must also complete the Louisiana radiation safety training and certification process through their employer before working with sources, and work as radiographer trainees under supervision.
  5. Year two onward: advanced UT. With conventional UT Level II in place, PAUT and TOFD training opens up the construction and advanced-inspection work that LNG and petrochemical owners increasingly specify.

Contractors who follow a plan like this can put trainees to productive work on turnarounds within weeks while building toward the certifications that clients audit. Atlantis can build the training schedule, the written practice and the exam programme around it. Level III services and written practices for Lake Charles NDT companies

Growing inspection contractors in Southwest Louisiana often need Level III capability quickly to bid work. Under SNT-TC-1A an outside Level III can be designated. Atlantis provides:

  • Written practice development aligned to client and code requirements: see written practice development.
  • Procedures for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET referencing ASME, API and client specifications.
  • Examinations prepared and graded by a Level III.
  • Audit support for owner-user and EPC contractor audits.
  • Corporate training programmes: see corporate NDT training.

Read SNT-TC-1A training and certification, then book a Level III consultation.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five environments: NDT lab, welding workshop, aircraft hangar, oil and gas site and storage tank. Lake Charles trainees will find the oil and gas site and storage tank scenarios closest to plant and LNG work.

The simulator is for practice only and does not replace hands-on training or the practical exam on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who oversees course content, examinations and certification support for Lake Charles clients. Level III candidates can review ASNT Level III training.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Lake Charles

How do I get NDT certified in Lake Charles?

Your employer certifies you under SNT-TC-1A after classroom training, documented experience, general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and outside Level III services.

Can I take NDT training online in Louisiana?

Yes. Theory and Level III preparation are available live online. Practicals are completed onsite. See online NDT training.

Is there an Atlantis NDT training centre in Lake Charles?

No. We have no physical centre in Lake Charles; training is delivered online and onsite at your facility.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on your employer's written practice. See the recommended hours and experience in the training requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Louisiana?

Yes. Louisiana requires anyone performing industrial radiography to hold a valid industrial radiographer certification recognised by LDEQ and to work under a licensed company. This is separate from NDT certification in RT.

What does NDT training cost in Lake Charles?

We quote on request, based on method, level, group size and delivery format. Request a Lake Charles training quote; we reply within one business day.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Lake Charles employers?

Yes, SNT-TC-1A is the dominant framework for NDT personnel on Gulf Coast refining, petrochemical, LNG and pipeline work, though clients may add their own requirements.

Do you offer API 510, 570 or 653 training?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based only. Our NDT courses cover the methods used during API inspections, but not the API inspector certifications themselves.

Which method should I learn first for LNG and plant work?

UT and RT are the core methods, with PT essential for stainless and cryogenic welds. PAUT and TOFD follow once conventional UT is solid.

Can you train our crew onsite around turnaround season?

Yes, onsite training is scheduled around your turnaround and construction calendar. See corporate NDT training.

Does my company need a written practice?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A requires one before certification. See written practice development.

How should I prepare for the UT Level II exam?

Use UT Level 2 practice questions and the Practical NDT simulator with structured training.

I work in a plant as a welder or fitter. Can I move into NDT in Lake Charles?

Yes, and many Southwest Louisiana technicians started that way. You need an employer willing to take you on as a trainee under its written practice, then classroom training and documented experience in each method. Plant experience and existing site access make you easier to place on turnaround work.

Can a Louisiana radiographer card be used in Texas?

Radiation safety certification rules differ by state, and reciprocity depends on the receiving state's regulations. Crews working across the Sabine River into Texas should check with both LDEQ and the Texas regulator, and their employer's radiation safety officer, before starting work.
